q: Why unmark a grid cell when backtracking out of it?
options: So a different path can use that cell later
why: The cell was only off-limits for the current path.

q: What does pruning mean in backtracking?
options: Stopping a branch as soon as it can't lead to a valid answer
why: Cutting dead branches early is what makes backtracking practical.

q: N-Queens: two queens at (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) share the "\" diagonal when…
why: Moving down-right keeps r − c constant; the other diagonal keeps r + c constant.

q: Word Search worst case, board m×n, word length L?
why: Each start cell explores up to 3 new directions per letter (it can't go back).

q: How many ways are there to partition "aab" into palindromes?
Word Search II: find MANY words on the same board. Improvement?
options: Put all words in a trie and run one DFS that follows the trie
why: The trie lets all words share one walk and prunes paths no word continues.
